text:
Maria: Heads-up — saw a small burst of OOMs on a Dedicated node during steady-state continuous batching. Not a full crash but evictions + request failures for ~30s window. Stack: kv-cache heavy workloads + long prefix generation.
Raj: Can you paste the timeline? suspect token-budgeting admission might be letting very long sequences in once KV occupancy high.
Maria: Timeline + brief profile: GPU mem climbs steadily, KV cache at ~84% capacity, then batch assembly adds a few <30k-token requests and we hit soft-evictor. Logs: `evictable=0.03, soft_headroom=-0.12` right before failures.
Oliver: That matches what I saw in the sim runs last week. When kv_fill > 80% we should tighten admission: either reduce max_tokens_per_batch or prefer short-seq-first.
Chris: Also noticed a perf regression in the last kernel selector tweak — for large KV workloads the int8 fused-kernel path is slightly slower (and higher mem) for long contexts. Maybe selector mis-routed some models? :thinking:
Anya: Oncall saw the alerts, I posted graphs in the incident thread: https://grafana/redwood/d/kv-oom/kv-pressure-2028 (p95 spiked).
perf-bot: Automated flamegraph attached: https://perf/reports/flame-2287654321 — hot spots in batch_assembler::merge_prefixes and kv::serialize_for_gpu.
Raj: Proposed short experiment: add an extra admission gate that enforces token_bucketing when kv_fill > 75%. Pseudoconfig: ```
batching:
  admission:
    kv_pressure_threshold: 0.75
    token_bucketing: true
    bucket_targets: [8, 32, 128] # prefer smaller buckets when pressured
    max_tokens_per_request: 8192
```
Maria: +1 for token_bucketing. We should also try a soft-eviction backoff: when eviction_rate > 0, reject or reroute batches with long-seq candidates.
Oliver: Implementation note: queue policy change should be cheap — sort ready queue by (seq_len, arrival_time) weighted by kv_fill factor. e.g., score = seq_len * (1 + kv_fill). That biases shorter sequences during pressure without global pause.
Chris: For kernel selector, add a fallback: if model_variant uses fused-int8 but kv_fill>70% and avg_seq_len>64, prefer the generic quantized kernel which has smaller transient allocations. Small switch (one flag) but need perf run.
Anya: Can someone run a repro? I have a node snapshot from the incident. Minimal repro steps if you need: `./tools/run_repro --snapshot s3://repro/2287654321 --load-kv --mix-traffic`.
Raj: I'll wire up a canary config with token_bucketing + queue-score and run 6h sim with mixed traffic. Will post results.
Maria: Thanks. Action items: Raj deploy proto canary, Chris add kernel-selector fallback flag behind experiment, Oliver implement queue scoring hook, Anya keep monitoring. If the canary looks good we flip for Dedicated pool only first. :shipit:
perf-bot: Note: when testing, enable `--trace-kv-allocs` to capture transient allocation spikes (helps correlate with flamegraphs).
Maria: Cool. Filing follow-up thread for rollout checklist after we have sim numbers.
Oliver: One more thought — add a short-circuit where requests referencing already-hot KV keys get a slightly higher admission priority (to preserve cache hits), but only when kv_fill < 90% to avoid reinforcing pressure.
Raj: Good nuance. We'll include both heuristics in the test matrix.
Anya: I'll keep PagerDuty on for the Dedicated pool tonight and mute noisy alerts if the canary is noisy.
Maria: End of thread — thanks y'all.
